papers.title: Sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems: an overnight non-invasive EEG study.
papers.summary: This study used a non-invasive EEG mask to compare sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems (communal stable vs. individual stalls) over four nights. Horses in the single stable setting showed increased REM sleep and lying-down frequency over time, while those in the large barn had longer lying episodes, and younger horses exhibited more REM sleep and complete sleep cycles than older horses.

papers.title: Neural and behavioral correlates of consciousness: the welfare consequences of fatal hypobaric and hypercapnic hypoxia in laboratory mice.
papers.summary: This study compared brain activity and behavior during fatal hypobaric and hypercapnic hypoxia in mice using EEG. Hypobaric hypoxia produced an early shift to delta frequency bands, suggesting an anesthetic-like state before loss of posture, potentially offering a more humane euthanasia method.

papers.title: Increased aperiodic offset and heightened alpha power characterize resting-state EEG activity in Parkinson's disease
papers.summary: This preprint reports that patients with Parkinson's disease off medication show increased aperiodic offset and alpha power in resting-state EEG compared to healthy controls, which replicated across different EEG systems. Aperiodic parameters also scaled with age and disease duration.

papers.title: Propofol-Facilitated Recovery Sleep Modulates Cognitive Function via Slow Oscillation-Spindle Coupling After Acute Sleep Deprivation in Rats.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of propofol-facilitated recovery sleep on cognitive function after acute sleep deprivation in rats, focusing on slow oscillation-spindle coupling. Propofol restored spatial and recognition memory, increased slow oscillation density, and improved phase-accurate SO-spindle coupling aligned to the up state, alongside a reduced NKCC1/KCC2 ratio.

papers.title: Multiple-Classifier Binary Convolutional Siamese Networks for Code-Modulated Visual Evoked Potential Classification.
papers.summary: This study proposes a multiple-classifier binary convolutional Siamese (MCBCS) network for single-trial c-VEP classification. The MCBCS achieved the highest mean accuracy (96.89%) in within-subject evaluation, outperforming other methods, and demonstrated the effectiveness of class-specific similarity learning for robust BCI decoding.

papers.title: Associations between EEG measures and clinical severity in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This study assessed associations between EEG/evoked potential measures and clinical severity in 77 individuals with CDKL5 deficiency disorder. Resting EEG background slowing (1/f slope and power ratios) correlated with greater symptom severity, but evoked potential measures did not.

papers.title: The Human Intracerebral EEG Platform: A Cloud-Based Trusted Research Environment for Collaborative SEEG Research in Epilepsy and Neuroscience.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and implementation of the Human Intracerebral EEG Platform (HIP), a cloud-based Trusted Research Environment for collaborative stereo-EEG (SEEG) research. The platform provides secure access, standardized BIDS-iEEG data organization, collaborative spaces, and analysis software, currently hosting 34 institutions and 10 projects.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of EEG Complexity Reveals Cortical Rigidity Associated with Pain Severity in Chronic Pain.
papers.summary: This study used normative modeling of EEG complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension) in chronic pain patients versus controls. More negative frontal complexity deviations were associated with higher pain intensity, even after adjusting for confounders, suggesting a potential marker for pain severity.

papers.title: Brain-Language Alignment During Naturalistic Reading and Its Disruption by Mind-Wandering
papers.summary: This study used EEG and eye-tracking during naturalistic reading to test brain-language alignment. Encoding models with contextual embeddings (e.g., BERT) showed significant alignment in alpha/low-beta power and fixation-related potentials; alignment was reduced during mind-wandering, indicating attention fluctuations affect neural language processing.

papers.title: Low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (0.5-5 Hz): effects on EEG band amplitude, interhemispheric coherence, and cognitive performance.
papers.summary: This crossover study tested low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (0.5-5 Hz) in healthy adults. 1 Hz stimulation increased interhemispheric coherence in several bands, while other frequencies reduced delta/alpha power, but no changes in cognitive performance were observed.

papers.title: Daily Bowel Movements are Associated with Stronger Gut-Brain Phase-Amplitude Coupling and Better Cognitive Performance
papers.summary: This study investigated the association between bowel movement frequency and gut-brain coupling in women by recording EEG and EGG. They found that women with daily bowel movements had stronger gut-brain phase-amplitude coupling and made fewer cognitive errors, with a path analysis suggesting faecal short-chain fatty acids mediate this coupling.

papers.title: Cognitive exertion reshapes resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan
papers.summary: This study examines how cognitive exertion affects resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan, finding that post-task recordings show widespread slowing of individual alpha peak frequency and age-dependent changes in the aperiodic exponent. These results demonstrate that these markers are state-dependent and post-task recordings may be useful for indexing individual differences.

papers.title: Wearable Morphology-Adaptive in-Ear Device With Active Cleansing Capability for Multimodal Health Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper reports a wearable in-ear device that self-adapts to ear canal geometry and performs active wax cleaning, enabling stable multimodal recording. It integrates EEG, ECG, and temperature sensors with wireless transmission, reducing sensor-skin impedance by 20%.

papers.title: Impact of stress on EEG functional connectivity during procedural learning.
papers.summary: This study examined the neurophysiological effects of stress on medical trainees during a procedural learning task using EEG functional connectivity. They found that stress increased functional connectivity compared to calm conditions, suggesting a potential neurophysiological signature of stress that could inform personalized educational interventions.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
papers.summary: Using simultaneous multi-region Neuropixels recordings in 35 mice, this preprint found that psilocybin selectively reconfigures burst firing, not mean firing rates, across cortex, thalamus, and hippocampus. These burst effects were largely abolished by ketanserin, indicating 5-HT2A receptor dependence.

papers.title: Time-frequency characteristics of scalp high-frequency oscillations provide complementary biomarkers in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome.
papers.summary: This study analyzed scalp high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) patients, comparing groups with hypsarrhythmia and interictal epileptiform discharges. HFO detection rates were significantly higher in hypsarrhythmia groups, with lower-frequency HFOs in hypsarrhythmia with ES, suggesting scalp HFOs as complementary biomarkers for assessing ictal states.

papers.title: Multidimensional Microstate Alterations and Interpretable Classification of Electrical Status Epilepticus During Sleep Using Multi-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: This study developed a microstate-centered multidimensional EEG framework to distinguish ESES patients from non-ESES epilepsy patients, revealing alterations in microstates B and C including prolonged duration, altered frequency, and reduced frequency chaos game representation entropy. A five-feature logistic regression model achieved promising exploratory discrimination, suggesting ESES involves more constrained and less flexible microstate dynamics.

papers.title: Inkjet-Printed Aqueous Graphene Suspensions on Flexible Substrates for Multimodal Wearable Continuous Health Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper presents inkjet-printed graphene electrodes on flexible PET substrates for multimodal wearable health monitoring. The electrodes demonstrated high conductivity, durability, and signal quality comparable to commercial gel electrodes, and were used to detect sleep and drowsiness in car drivers.

papers.title: Event-Wise Stability of Patient-Specific EEG-MEG Deep Learning Spike Detection in Clinical MEG
papers.summary: This study developed a patient-specific EEG-MEG deep learning detector for interictal epileptiform discharges and evaluated event-wise stability across models. Adding EEG to MEG improved event-wise positioning, while MEG remained dominant in MEG-dominant cases, supporting multimodal patient-specific detection.

papers.title: Personality Trait Modulated Panic Emotional Arousal and Physiological Responses in Underground Spaces: A Virtual Reality and Multimodal Measurement Study.
papers.summary: This study developed a personality-modulated panic dynamics framework using virtual reality evacuation experiments with multimodal physiological measurements. They found that personality traits influence physiological responses during panic, and constructed a Panic Composite Index to quantify individual panic intensity.

papers.title: Altered early cortical EEG maturation and its relationship to language development in Down syndrome
papers.summary: This study analyzed longitudinal resting-state EEG from children with Down syndrome and typically developing children, finding altered maturation of aperiodic and periodic spectral features in Down syndrome. In Down syndrome, a spectral dimension was associated with verbal developmental quotient rather than chronological age, indicating altered relationship between cortical organization and language development.

papers.title: Multisensory processing of emotional cues in individuals with social anxiety: Evidence from event-related potentials.
papers.summary: This study examined emotional processing in social anxiety disorder using EEG during a forced-choice emotion identification task with visual, auditory, and audiovisual stimuli. They found that the social anxiety group had larger P3a amplitudes for auditory and audiovisual angry stimuli, indicating an interpretation bias at late processing stages.

papers.title: EEG coherence signatures of sport-specific motor imagery in elite freestyle skiing aerials athletes.
papers.summary: This study characterized EEG coherence during sport-specific motor imagery in elite freestyle skiing aerials athletes. They found that high-difficulty imagery elicited stronger theta-band coherence over right-hemisphere connections, and correct judgments were associated with higher high-alpha coherence.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and autonomic effects of Cognitive Remediation Therapy in schizophrenia: a randomized controlled EEG-GSR study.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial examined the effects of Cognitive Remediation Therapy (CRT) on neurophysiological, autonomic, and cognitive outcomes in schizophrenia patients. CRT significantly increased P300 amplitude and frontal midline theta power, reduced skin conductance responses to negative stimuli, and improved working memory, emotion recognition, and clinical symptoms.

papers.title: Brain-Behavior Relationships in Children With ADHD: Resting-state EEG Networks Underlying Executive Function and Neurological Soft Signs.
papers.summary: This study examined sex-stratified brain-behavior relationships in pediatric ADHD using resting-state EEG graph-theoretical connectivity measures, finding sex-specific network alterations: lower local connectivity in ADHD girls and right centro-temporal inhibitory-circuit deficits in boys versus antero-posterior sensory-gating alterations in girls. Brain-behavior correlations emerged density-dependently, particularly in upper alpha and beta bands in ADHD girls, potentially explaining diagnostic camouflage.

papers.title: Neurocognitive Recovery After Liver Transplantation Is Driven by Metabolite-mediated Reactivation of Cortical Networks.
papers.summary: This prospective study of 21 liver transplant patients found significant neurocognitive improvements and EEG changes (increased alpha1/beta power, enhanced connectivity, altered microstate dynamics) post-transplant, alongside reduced plasma GFAP and elevated S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine (MTA). In vitro and in vivo experiments showed MTA attenuates inflammatory neurotoxicity and preserves neuronal function, suggesting a role in neuroprotection and cognitive recovery.

papers.title: Distinct electrophysiology and dopaminergic modulation of medium spiny neurons across divisions of the tail striatum and the dorsolateral striatum.
papers.summary: This study characterized the electrophysiological properties of medium spiny neurons in the tail striatum compared to the dorsolateral striatum using whole-cell patch clamping. They found TS-MSNs are more depolarized, have lower rheobase, and show weaker dopamine modulation, with heterogeneity across divisions.

papers.title: Perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation and EEG biomarkers of sleep improvement after gynecologic laparoscopy: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This paper describes a randomized controlled trial protocol to evaluate whether perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reduces postoperative sleep disturbance in gynecologic laparoscopy patients. The trial will integrate continuous EEG monitoring to explore mechanistic EEG biomarkers.

papers.title: Contemporary Sedation Strategies for Mechanical Ventilation: Balancing Patient Outcomes, Delirium Prevention, and Early Recovery.
papers.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
papers.summary: This review examines contemporary sedation strategies for mechanically ventilated patients, highlighting the shift from deep sedation to lighter protocols to reduce delirium and improve outcomes. It discusses pharmacological agents, monitoring tools, and non-pharmacologic interventions, emphasizing structured approaches like the ABCDEF bundle.

papers.title: Evolving epileptic activity under focal rhythmic Delta activity: insights from simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG in six patients with intracranial hematoma to assess whether focal rhythmic delta activity (RDA) on scalp EEG reflects intracranial epileptic activity. They found that while focal RDA on scalp EEG appeared in all cases, intracranial RDA appeared earlier, and spikes, electrographic seizures, and high-frequency oscillations were often not detected on scalp EEG, suggesting that focal RDA may indicate growing epileptic activity and a target for antiseizure therapy.

papers.title: Left-sided Inhibition Deficit and right-sided Hyperexcitability in Treatment Resistant Bipolar Depression: A TMS-EEG study
papers.summary: This TMS-EEG study compared short-latency intracortical inhibition in treatment-resistant bipolar depression and healthy controls. It found reduced left-sided inhibition and right-sided hyperexcitability in patients, with right-sided global SICI partly normalized by lithium.

papers.title: EFS-NET: EEG-fNIRS multi-scale fusion network based on spatial calibration.
papers.summary: The paper presents EFS-Net, an end-to-end multi-scale fusion network integrating EEG and fNIRS for hybrid brain-computer interfaces, using spatial calibration to align delayed hemodynamic responses. On two public datasets, it achieved classification accuracies of 77.71% and 81.69%, surpassing state-of-the-art unimodal and traditional fusion models.

papers.title: HD-tDCS modulation of the DLPFC-HPC-EC pathway to enhance working memory in schizophrenia: a TMS-EEG Study.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial tested a single session of HD-tDCS targeting the left DLPFC in schizophrenia patients. It significantly improved working memory accuracy and reaction times, with TMS-EEG showing reduced excitability in EC and HPC, and mediation analyses implicating the DLPFC-HPC-EC pathway.

papers.title: Electroencephalogram Utilization, Epileptiform Findings, and Associated Factors Among Children with Epilepsy in Southwestern Uganda: A 5-Year Retrospective Record Review.
papers.summary: This retrospective record review of 427 children with epilepsy in southwestern Uganda found that only 34.9% had undergone EEG, with epileptiform EEGs in 68.5% of those. Female sex and generalized seizures were independently associated with higher likelihood of epileptiform EEGs, highlighting the need for increased EEG use and training.

papers.title: Effects of exercise interventions on EEG alpha power across different populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 randomized controlled trials (497 participants) found that exercise interventions were associated with greater EEG alpha-band power than control conditions (Hedges' g = 1.23), but with considerable heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals, indicating substantial uncertainty across settings.

papers.title: Reliability of Bonini's semiological classification in frontal lobe seizures: A video-EEG based study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This study evaluated the reliability of Bonini's semiological classification in frontal lobe seizures using video-EEG recordings from 33 patients, finding excellent intraobserver reliability and substantial interobserver agreement. The classification showed correlations with neuroimaging and surgical outcomes in a subset of patients, supporting its utility as a reproducible framework for presurgical evaluation.

papers.title: Education Research: Development of a Workplace-Based Assessment to Enhance EEG Interpretation Skills for Medical Students.
papers.summary: This prospective study developed and evaluated a workplace-based assessment (WBA) for medical students during a 2-week EEG elective, involving 79 WBAs with 20 students. The tool was feasible and educationally valuable, with a significant decrease in high-level assistance needed from week 1 to week 2, indicating its effectiveness in enhancing EEG interpretation skills.

papers.title: Machine learning and molecular docking-driven identification of novel umami peptides from pea protein and electroencephalography (EEG) neural mechanisms analysis of their umami-enhancing effects.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and molecular docking to identify novel umami peptides from pea protein, and validated their umami-enhancing effects using sensory evaluation, electronic tongue, and EEG analysis. The peptides enhanced umami perception, elicited specific neural oscillations in theta, alpha, and beta bands, and showed strong activation in parietal and parieto-occipital regions, with key receptor-binding sites identified.

papers.title: New-Onset Convulsive Status Epilepticus Temporally Associated With Accidental Inhalation of Billygoat Weed (Ageratum conyzoides) Smoke: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 76-year-old man who developed new-onset convulsive status epilepticus approximately five minutes after inhaling smoke from burning Ageratum conyzoides (billygoat weed). Extensive investigations were unremarkable, and the patient recovered fully, suggesting a possible association between smoke inhalation and seizures.

papers.title: A Mobile Electrophysiology System with Mixed Reality Virtual Screens for Pediatric Ablation.
papers.summary: The paper reports the first use of a fully mobile electrophysiology system integrated with mixed reality virtual displays for pediatric catheter ablation, successfully performing radiofrequency ablation in a 9-year-old with atrioventricular nodal reentry tachycardia. This demonstrates feasibility of mobile, mixed-reality-enabled EP systems to expand procedural access while maintaining clinical performance.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
